parole.testo: Borrowed from German aphoristisch, from Ancient Greek ἀφορῐστικος (aphorĭstikos).
Borrowed from German Askese, from Ancient Greek ἄσκησις (áskēsis).
Borrowed from German Ballistik. Cognate with French balistique. Modern formation from Ancient Greek βαλέειν (baléein) similar to how akustik was formed from ἀκούειν (akoúein).

From German Chromosom, ultimately from Ancient Greek χρῶμα (khrôma, “colour”) + σῶμα (sôma, “body”).

parole.significato: onomatopoeia (a word that sounds like what it represents)
parole.testo: From German Onomatopoetikon, from Ancient Greek ὀνοματοποιία (onomatopoiía), a compound of ὄνομα (ónoma, “name”) + ποιέω (poiéō, “to make”).
Borrowed from German Polytop. By surface analysis, poly- + -top, from Ancient Greek τόπος (tópos, “region; area”).
Borrowed from German Pykniker, from Ancient Greek πυκνός (puknós).
From German Thermit, from Ancient Greek θερμός (thermós, “heat”) + -it.

parole.significato: hydrophobia, as a symptom of rabies
parole.testo: Compound of vatten (“water”) + -u- + skräck (“fright”), calque of German Wasserscheu (“fear of water”), ultimately from Ancient Greek ὑδροφοβία (hudrophobía, “hydrophobia”). Likely named after the rabies afflicted's inability to swallow liquid. First attested in 1738.
